ui_bugs.component: Header (on inner pages: BlogPost / ServicePage / LegalPage / NotFound)
ui_bugs.issue: Invisible header nav + logo at initial page load (scrollY=0). Header is `bg-transparent` with `onDark = !scrolled` → nav links render `rgba(255,255,255,0.85)` and Logo renders `light`. But on inner pages `<main className='pt-[76px]'>` pushes the dark hero to y=76, so the element directly behind the 76px-tall fixed header is `div.bg-paper` = rgb(250,250,250). Result: white text on near-white background, contrast ratio ~1.05:1 (WCAG fail). Verified via elementsFromPoint: behind nav link = 'DIV.bg-paper min-h-screen bg=rgb(250,250,250)'; dark hero SECTION.bg-brand-ink starts at top=76. Home page is unaffected (hero image sits under the header). Affects all 5 blog articles, 4 service pages, 3 legal pages and 404. Header becomes readable only after scrolling >30px (switches to bg-white/80 + text-brand-ink).

issues: Header navigation links and logo wordmark are effectively invisible (white on rgb(250,250,250)) until the user scrolls. Suggested fix: pass isHome/onDark=false for non-home routes, or force the solid `bg-white/80 + text-brand-ink` header variant when isHome === false, or extend the dark hero behind the header instead of using main pt-[76px].

action_items: Fix header contrast on inner pages: when isHome is false (or when the header overlays bg-paper), render the solid header variant (bg-white/80 + text-brand-ink + Logo light={false}) instead of the transparent/white-text variant, so nav links and the logo are legible at scroll position 0.
critical_code_review_comments: Header.jsx derives `onDark = !scrolled` purely from scroll position and ignores the `isHome` prop it already receives. On inner pages the area behind the header is bg-paper (light), so the dark-mode styling is wrong at scrollY=0. `onDark` should be `isHome && !scrolled`.

The 76px header height is duplicated as a magic value in ServicePage.jsx:99, LegalPage.jsx:31 and BlogPost.jsx:82 (`pt-[76px]`) and again in Header.jsx (`h-[76px]`). Extract to a single constant / Tailwind theme token to avoid drift.

Positive: content is fully centralised in src/lib/content.js (CONTACT/BRAND/BLOG), so the rename, domain and email changes propagated consistently with no hardcoded leftovers — no DRY violations found for this iteration's changes.

rca_of_the_issue: Root cause: Header.jsx computes `const onDark = !scrolled;` using only window.scrollY, even though the component already accepts an `isHome` prop. The header is `fixed` and `bg-transparent` when not scrolled. On the home page a dark hero image sits beneath the header so white text is legible, but BlogPost.jsx, ServicePage.jsx and LegalPage.jsx wrap their content in `<main className='pt-[76px]'>` inside a `div.bg-paper` container — that 76px padding is exactly the header height, so the dark hero section begins at y=76 and the light bg-paper (rgb(250,250,250)) is what renders behind the header. White text (rgba(255,255,255,0.85)) over rgb(250,250,250) yields ~1.05:1 contrast, making nav links and the logo wordmark invisible. Reproduction: open https://saudi-services-hub-2.preview.emergentagent.com/blog/work-visa-fees without scrolling and inspect the header. Mitigation: change to `const onDark = isHome && !scrolled;` (and pass Logo light={onDark}), or make the inner-page heroes extend behind the fixed header instead of offsetting with pt-[76px].
